Otolaryngology · published research

Otitis media

In rats, dual-wavelength LEDs reduced inflammatory measures in an LPS model and suppressed biofilm and inflammation in an MRSA model. Neither study establishes clinical benefit or hearing preservation in patients.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In rats, dual-wavelength LEDs reduced inflammatory measures in an LPS model and suppressed biofilm and inflammation in an MRSA model. Neither study establishes clinical benefit or hearing preservation in patients.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Otitis media category contains two South Korean preclinical publications. Both are rat studies; one also includes an in-vitro cell arm. No human clinical study is listed, and the two experiments address distinct inflammatory or infectious models.

Human and clinical evidence

Ko et al. studied dual 655- and 842-nm LED treatment in an LPS-induced rat otitis-media model. Treatment reduced middle-ear inflammatory thickness and cytokines compared with LPS controls. The same paper reported lower inflammatory cytokines and MAPK signaling in cultured human middle-ear epithelial cells and macrophages, without observed cytotoxicity in the tested conditions (2023, DOI 10.3389/fbioe.2023.1099574, PubMed). Ko et al. later treated rats with MRSA biofilm otitis media through the ear canal for 30 minutes daily over five days, beginning seven days after inoculation. They reported reduced biofilm and inflammation (2025). Neither paper tests PBM in patients, and neither demonstrates improved hearing or prevention of complications.

Animal evidence

The two rat models cover LPS-induced inflammation and MRSA biofilm infection. Outcomes are tissue inflammation and bacterial biofilm rather than clinical hearing recovery. Animal results cannot determine whether light can reach the relevant structures safely or effectively in people.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

The 2023 paper included cultured human middle-ear epithelial cells and macrophages. Dual-wavelength treatment reduced inflammatory cytokine and MAPK measures without detected cytotoxicity under the reported conditions. This is one in-vitro arm within a publication, not a separate clinical study.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The 2023 study used 655- and 842-nm LEDs. In the 2025 MRSA model, light was delivered through the ear canal for 30 minutes per day for five days after infection was established. The wavelength and exposure conditions are model-specific; the database records do not establish a clinically optimized dose or safe human delivery schedule.

Interpretation

The two studies support further preclinical investigation of inflammatory and biofilm pathways. They provide no direct evidence that PBM treats human otitis media.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for treating human otitis media
Publications and records2 publications, both rat studies.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Two South Korean publications tested red and near-infrared LED treatment in rat models. One also included cultured human middle-ear epithelial cells and macrophages. Findings on inflammation and biofilm are preclinical, with no human treatment trial. Replication should test safety and hearing outcomes in clinically relevant models before patient efficacy is inferred.
